body: You can reach to this place by a vehicle or can walk to the top of the hill up to the Buddhist temple. When you reach there you can see the beauty of the Nuwaraeliya town and surroundings.
title: Easy access from the Nuwaraeliya City

body: Small walk up to the temple, from there you have a beautiful view of Nuwara Eliya. From there it goes on a steep bit
title: Nice viewpoint

body: Many can't find their way to the viewing platform, on Mt. There it is (photo). Even guides often don't know. In front of us, the Pole and the guide were running through the bushes, and then they just turned around and left.
title: Way to the viewing platform.

body: Single Tree Hill is the 10th tallest mountain in Sri Lanka and is right in the heart of the Nuwara Eliya town. The google map directions are accurate. There is a temple on the way to the summit. Upto the this temple, the road, running through the Pedro tea Estate, is wide enough for two SUVs to pass and is in very good conditon. There is ample parking at the temple. (Things might be different on a poya day when the temple has devotees.) From the temple, there is a wide gravel road up to the summit, which is in terrible conditon, even a tuk won't offer to take you up..The summit is not too far, but due to the slight but continous ascent and the hard gravel road, it took us about 30 minutes to get to the top. The summit will be a bit of an anti climax. There are some telecom towers at the top, so the area is fenced off. Plus there is no view due to the shrubs. And..... there is no "single tree";)We were told by a seasoned hiker, that there is a path from this summit to Shanthipura. But we couldnt find it and there were no sign boards. When we visited last year Oct- Nov, there was a strong mist, so there was absolutely no view from anywhere. Nevertheless, we enjoyed the weather and the short hike. This year we visited again in October and there was a very clear view of the Nuwara Eliya town and the surrounding areas from the temple and on the way up through the tea estate. While we had a good time hiking, I would say the experience was "average" unless you consider climbing the 10th tallest mountain in Sri Lanka as a bucket list item. And the temple too may not warrant a visit on its own as it is still partly constructed. (Also construction seems to have come to a standstill from last year to this year).But if you are already in Nuwara Eliya and bored at the hotel or wants to burn some extra calories gained from the hotel food, as was the case for us, this is an ideal short excursion;)
title: The shortest climb to the 10th tallest mountain....

body: Some time ago I reached this place with my wife. This place with a good view of the city is about 1 km away from Swayambhu temple. There is also swing of rope.in this place which is perfect for pictures.Restaurants and hotels are also nearby for lunch. Enjoyed visiting this place where domestic and foreign tourists also come
title: Nice view

body: Require 4 wheel drive. We had to do hard trek about 45 minutes. The views were magnificent. A little clarification is required: Single Tree here refers to mobile towers at the Summit :(. It's possible approach from Town also. We couldn't get view from the summit as it was fenced. We couldn't explore further as due to thick fog
title: SINGLE TREE HILL

body: We were expecting to summit to a viewpoint with an iconic tree but there’s no such place. The whole area up the mountain from the temple is known as single tree hill. We drove and parked at the temple and walked from there on - approximately half hour uphill (not steep so easily doable with kids). You end up at a telecom / radio tower - behind that there was a pathway through a forest stretch that leads to few bushes ... there was a path way down but we didn’t know where it leads to and since we had to get to our vehicles at the temple we took the same route downhill. It’s a decent walk if you have nothing else to do.
title: There’s no single tree!

body: Single Tree Hill is a must visit if you are holidaying in Nuwara Eliya It's a 30 mins drive through the Tea Estate to the top of the Mountain from the Welimada Road turn on Single Tree Road on 4 Wheel Drive right to the top and if a Two Wheel Drive then you have to park the Vehicle 1000m before the Top of the Hill and if it's walking to the top from the Welimada Road turn off then it would take approx 90minutes as advised by the locals in the Area We went on our Vehicle upto 500m before reaching the hill which is now mounted with three large Communications Towers of the mobile operators The view from the Top of the Mountain unravels the spectacular views of the entire Nuwara Eliya Town including the beauty of the Pidurutalagala Mountains, Gregory Lake Landscapes & Haggala Mountains clearly and with so many other scenic breathtaking views from the Top and on the way to the Hill and on a clear day part of the Adams Peak and Sunset views has been visible as per the locals living in Nuwara Eliya.This is the 7th largest mountain in Sri Lanka with a height of 6890 feet above meansea Level and what's unique is that it's easily accessible and we were so glad that we made it to the top during our weekend stay in Little England.
title: Spectacular Scenic Views of Nuwara Eliya from the Single Tree Hill

body: Excellent Service fromUsman and Dewni Special thanks to Chef Prasad Who recommend our food inthe display Food is very tasty and the service is next level Nirash attend to ourtable all the time thank you. Definetely will come again
title: Excellent Service and Food

body: If you are looking for a hidden trekking path in Nuwaraeliya, this is the place to go. You can travel to Single tree by a tuk and the there is a path to Shanthipura viewpoint through jungle. You will see some unseen views in Nuwaraeliya and it is really mesmerizing.
title: Single Tree to Shanthipura Trek in Nuwaraeliya

body: Really nice and easy walk up to the top, through a temple and tea plantations, with a great view at the top.From there, there is a single track going through vegetables tarraces and a nice direct of tall nilgiris, up to the wonderful Tea plantations of Shantipura. Much more quiet. From Shantipura, you can take a tuk-tuk to go back to Nuwara Elya.
title: Quietness and great views of Nuwara Elya and Shantipura

body: You can park your vehicle at the Single Tree Buddhist temple. Please try to tell them about your visit to add some respect. From the temple you have to walk. It is fun. We walked with our two kids. You can have a spectacular view of Nuwara Eliya town from there. The top of the hill is closed due to security reasons since there are communication towers. The climate and environment change rapidly when you go up.
title: A cool place with some jungle experience

body: Walking up from the buddhist temple you’ll discover the beautiful views of Nuwara Eliya. Don’t expect too much. On the top we did not really find the viewpoint, grass has grown that high that you can hardly enjoy the views. But if you turn right near the fence and walk along it you can find the place to enjoy the lake view. Good tracking though)
title: Good tracking & lake view

body: Just 5 minutes drive from the number Eliya city down nuwara Eliya -badulla road is single tree hill road .drive up to the Buddhist temple and walk up to the view points. Probably the best view over the city ,lake and the surrounding areas. Highly recommended
title: WHAT A VIEW

body: Single Tree Hill is situated at Nuweraeliya town and it is considered as the 10th highest mountain (2105 m) in Sri Lanka. It is just a small hike from Nuweraeliya-Badulla road. There is a gravel road which is good for a four wheel and I would like to recommend to walk along the road as it is scenic. You can enjoy the view towards Piduruthalagala towers, Gregory Lake and Hakgala mountain. Swarnagiri Temple is situated at middle of the path and summit of the mountain is occupied by communication towers. Sri Pada and Hatton area can be viewed from the summit of the mountain. We spent about 1 hour to hike Single Tree Hill mountain.
title: Small hike from Nuweraeliya Town

body: It is a nice location,you can see part of Nuwara Eliya Town and can see the beauty of Gregory Lake. Hard to drive by a car . Recommend 4*4 vehicle
title: Nice Location

body: Rooms are not great. Saw some foreign families who’ve got better rooms but not the locals. The rooms were lacking comfort. Food is great and fresh!
title: Trip to Nuwara eliya

body: We had not planned to climb this hill but we were drawn by the glistening green leaves of the tea bushes. Half way to the top is a Buddhist temple which can be a rest stop for the weary or the final stop for the unprepared. There are beautiful views of the town, the race track and Lake Gregory. Allot around 2 hours for a leisurely hike. Be sure to bring your own water, energy bars, and protection from the sun.
title: Hike in a tea plantation

body: Hiked the single tree hill over the Christmas break and found it rather refreshing. The best thing about this hill is the location, it's on the nuwara Eliya town so you dont have to struggle to get to it and u can pretty much walk as much as you like and hike down. The view is amazing
title: View point

body: Small Mountain. Great View. Serene Buddhist Temple.Visited here in March with family as a detour compared to the options available @ that moment. Our cabbie offered us to take here just for a different experience.The roads were pretty narrow for our Honda Sedan to maneuver, but, manageable.On reaching the top, the view was breathtaking! You can see the Gregory lake, the lush tea plantations and the Nuwara Eliya topography from here.The temple is made beautifully and maintained very well by the priests there. A huge, real-sized elephant statue is also made.Definitely worth spending 15-20 mins here. Takes 10 mins to reach there from the main road.Date of Experience : March 2019.
title: Small Mountain. Great View. Serene Buddhist Temple.

body: If you like a good hike this is the place in Nuwara Eliya. Can drive upto Swarnagiri maha viharaya and from there can hike upto the top of the hill. Wear comfortable shoes. There's nothing much to do on top of the hill except for the telecom antennas. But you will see the entire town from here. It is a marvellous view.
title: Vintage point in Nuwara Eliya

body: We took this walk in a the start of a big day of walking so glad we did this second as we could not have done it if we left it to last.So after a trip to the post office we set off a great walk of a bot 2 klm which has you sitting at the top at 2,100 metres above sea level after negating the path and then a resonably short gravel path walk.Make sure you go through the narrow path between the towers once you reach the top for great views of the lake and steep tea plantations.Although I did have to top a few times up due to smoking earlier in life I was a great ad for the non smoking campaign (seriously don't smoke) make sure you take plenty of water, wear comfortable shoes.I recommend this walk to everyone and I can only imagine it very early when it is a clear as a bell.
title: A Kodak moment aka a great photo opportunity for those younger than me

body: An easy walk up a steep hill banked by tea plantations on both sides. Parts of the road are paved and there is some loose gravel closer to the top. Lots of small birds, if that’s your thing. If you do this walk, do visit the temple, it’s worth a look, then continued up the hill for a panoramic view of the city abd Gregory Lake. You could take a tuk-tuk up to the temple but the walk is easy enough and it’s a very relaxing way to take in some nature and scenery.
title: Peaceful walk (or jog) up a steep hill

body: The run up Single Tree offers about two kilometres of steady hills on a smooth road followed by another 500m+ of much rockier terrain. You need to be careful with your footing once past the temple up to the final gate. It takes about 20min all the way up and then 15min down as part of a cautious holiday workout. It is lovely to run in cooler weather in Sri Lanka through some tea plantations and the view from the top is great.
title: Quick Strava fix for runners

body: Really amazing for a hiking up to more then 3 km approximately then from the top of the hill can see the full town view and also a clear view of Pedro mountain the highest mountain in SriLanka
title: Hiking with a view of nuwaraeliya

body: We did a 4 1/2 hours walk with a guide. His knowledge of the area and tracks was fantastic. The different terrain we went through was amazingly! We thoroughly enjoyed this adventure!
title: Well worth doing

body: On the way to the top of the hill, you can visit Swarnagiri Maha Viharaya & can see Sri Padaya. On the top, you can see the very beautiful scenery of the city & Gregory Lake.
title: City Hike.

body: Allow a good 2 hours round trip and wear sturdy shoes... Best with a friend or a local guide... NOT the best for solo females. We had no issues but I would not go up alone at dusk just tube on the safe side. The views are stunning and well worth the effort.
title: Stunning sunset hike

body: Just of the main nuwaraeliya Badulla road you will find a small road call single tree hill. Once you reach the top there is a small temple. And the view is amazing ..
title: Great view

body: We knew it might happen, but sure enough, a cloud blew in before we made it to the top of the hill, and we had no real view to speak of. It was a pleasant enough walk down, but since we had climbed a different mountain that morning, we had taken a tuktuk up this hill. Not much to see at the top, so if you can't see far it's not quite worth the stop.
title: Go when it's clear

body: Spectacular views and peaceful temple awaits at this beauty spot, not too challenging to walk and easy terrain to walk on. Well worth the short hike. Would recommend
title: Well worth the walk

body: It is worth the climb if you have the time available, the view from the top is pretty (although we did not see the single tree). Easy walk to the top, especially if you are transported to the temple. Took us about 20-25 mins with a 10 & 7 year old
title: Worth the climb

body: One of the easiest treck in nuwara, this starts from a temple and you reach to top in 20 min is you are on right path. Amazing view of lake from top
title: Trecking

body: This is comparatively easiest treck in nuwara eliya. There is temple and walk of 25 mins to top of the hill which offers great view of city and lake
title: Hill view

body: This is one of the mountains among 10th highest list. On the way you can worship the temple and there is a another beautiful view there. On the top you can see whole Nuwaraeliya town and suburbs.
title: Single Tree hike

body: The walk is lovely, but don't do it alone, particularly if you are female.Whilst I was walking up Single Tree Hill in May 2018, I met two policemen who stopped me and said to be careful as there had been an attack and they had still not caught the person.Please note: I have posted this review of my personal experience of Single Tree more than once - I live in Nuwara Eliya and walk here most weeks and it has not been posted any of the times - I don't know why
title: Be careful

body: We started at the temple (got 4 min drive up) and from there it's a nice easy 20 min stroll up to the top. Nice scenic views along the way, overlooking much of the area. View at the top is pretty much the same as the view along the way. Didn't manage to identify any "single tree" :) recommended!
title: Nice walk for a view over the city

body: This was my first full day in Nuwara Eliya so i left my guest house after breakfast, and reached the turn-off by the SW corner of the race track by 9 am and started the climb up the road to the top of the hill. I think it was about 4 kms through a tea estate and eventually the road turned into a track before reaching several communication towers. Then there was a path that led me around the fenced compounds which eventually led to the "Single Tree", but i guess there were at least three trees there now, surrounded by tea trees. The single tree was easy to recognise as there were orange scarves tied to the tree and a few figures at the base, which served as a shrine. From this vantage point there was a wonderful view of the town, racetrack, Gregory Lake and surrounding hills and it was well worth spending 15 minutes up here. There seemed to be another path leading back to the small road, but after a while i had to retrace my steps as it became impossible to follow.
title: Hike up Single Tree Hill for an amazing view

body: We drove up to the temple and from there you can get good views of the countryside, Eliya and the tea plantations. We did not walk to the top as with the intermittent rain I doubt we could have gotten a better view. this site is purely a viewpoint and nothing else. There is nothing else around!
title: Good views of the Countryside from here.

body: This is one of the best location to view the Nuwara Eliya. The road is sealed up to the Single Tree Hill monastery.You could take a taxi or hire car up to the monastery & park there. Past the monastery, it is all gravel road, would not recommend taking a car unless it is 4x4. The walk from the monastery is about 20 mins. On the top of the hill is a telecom tower. Towards the end of the walk, you will come across wired fences, go past the fence & you will be able to get spectacular views of Nuwara Eliya, the lake, mountains and tea fields.
title: Best vantage point to observe the beauty of Nuwara Eliya

body: It was just after some rain had cleared so the too was shrouded in mist but I went up anyway. The road first winds gently through tea fields and past a temple then becomes a steeper, rougher road. Shortly before the top, you can see a small blue shrine above on the right. Look for some rough stairs and you can follow these to a bench in front of the towers. Didn’t help me that day as I couldn’t see anything from the top but from lower down the road I spectacular views of southern Nuwara Eliya, the lake, mountains and tea fields.
title: Misty mountain walk

body: To start the walk head out of town, at roundabout take Badulla Road then watch out for Single Tree Road on the right after 800m. From there it's simple - the road snakes up through a tea plantation, past a temple and towards the masts. Once you get to the masts there's a narrow track between two fences that takes you to the view over to Gregory Lake. There's a seat to have a rest. From there we headed back to the main track, then continued along the crest of the hill on a narrow track, which eventually drops at some huts. We cut right here and joined Unique View Road back down the hill, with a beer stop at Qantara Hotel, which has a terrace with a view! Nice to do the loop rather than up and down. Even saw monkeys along the crest walk.
title: Hike with a view

body: This is a pleasant easy walk to the top of a hill overlooking Nuwara Eliya. Although it ranks as one of the highest mountains in Sri Lanka, it is only about an hour's steady walk from the town through tea plantations. Keep a look out for Barking Deer. The single tree has long since gone and has been replaced by telecommunications masts, but with your back to them, you have great views. Unlike Horton Plains and World's End, it is free!
title: Watch the sun rise over the lake

body: The trek to Single Tree Hill is not challenging and is quite picturesque, giving you views of the city as you walk along tea plantations for some time. The entry point is a small lane right beside Cliffton Hotel. The final point is reached by taking stairs to the right where the Google Maps path ends. Although the summit isn't as amazing as you would think, the trek is worth doing.
title: Beautiful views of the city

body: The most challenging part was finding the entry point to Single Tree Hill Road. It is off Queen Elizabeth Road, about 50 from Haddon Hill Road, and next to Clifton Inn. Once you are on that road, there can be no mistake about how to proceed.The road starts as a narrow asphalt road winding itself up to a beautiful monastery, about half way to the top. It continues as a narrow dirt road which can be driven with a high clearance vehicle or tuk-tuk. Unfortunately there is a lot of trash dumping along the way.We walked up and down, which took about 45 minutes each way, with plenty of stops for taking in the marvelous views of the tea landscape below us.There is no need to walk to the very end, as bushes obstruct the view in that section.
title: How to find the trail

body: This is a little of the beaten track, but it's a great little walk up a hill between the tea fields.We took a shortcut down towards the tea fields.
title: Great walk

body: This is a two hours long walk (there and back) through a hilly tea field in Nuwara Eliya that provides great views over the town and surrounding tea plantations. I really enjoyed it. It was a bit hard to find the path though (yes, there is one!).Go along the Queen Elisabeth road, then turn right to the Haddon Hill road all the way to Teabush hotel, where the road end. The Teabush is fenced and you need to go around the fenced area from its right side. There is a narrow slippery path. It is disappearing at times, but try to keep following it, it zig-zags all the way to the top. If you lose sight of it, just go up among the bushes (thats what I did half of the way as I didnt know about the path) - you will eventually come across it again. Wouldnt recommend this walk with children, but its a nice outing if you have a few hours to kill. The view is brilliant.
title: Great view of Nuwara Eliya

body: The view of the city and of the surrounding hills was amazing. It is a long but not difficult hike to reach the top. Sometimes the mist can cover the view but I was lucky that day because it faded quickly.On the way to the top there is also a small temple
title: The most beatiful view of the city

body: Best place to get a whole view of Nuwara Eliya. You can enjoy a quick hike through tea bushes and a bit of a jungle. The views along the hike a incredible and on a clear morning, you are able to see the top of Adam's Peak, just as you pass the temple (Picture is attached here). This hike was what I enjoyed most about my visit to Nuwara Eliya. Definite must do if you're visiting Nuwara Eliya.
title: Easy Hike with Incredible Views

body: At the top, there is a temple. You can have some great views of Nuwara-Eliya city from here. If you are not coming by a private vehicle, there is a bit of climbing to do. The road to the top is not at the best condition. But, it should be manageable, even it is somewhat narrow. Parking is also available in the temple.
title: Great to Have Fascinating Views of the City and Worship at the same Time

body: It was a bit difficult to find the starting point when we walked from the centre of the town. We passed a tourist information close to the bus station, but the "map" they offered was not very specific. The hike goes through tea plantations and is quite easy, but steeper when you approach the top of the hill. Nice view from the top (2100 all) until it started to rain. It seems to be optional paths to get down, but since they were not marked, we decided to return the way we came.
title: Good hike to the top

body: I thoroughly enjoyed the walk up Single Tree Hill this week. However on the way back down just above the temple, I was attacked by a local man with a knife wanting to rape me. I was in hiking gear - trousers, boots, Tshirt, rucksack so nothing provocative. Fortunately I practice martial arts, so was confident and able to diffuse the situation without any physical violence. It could have been a very different story. Single women - seriously reconsider doing this walk alone.
title: Important Warning!

body: Quite a fast (1h30 at most) walk in the middle of the tea plantations, with a fantastic view on Nuwara Eliya and its surroundings. Easy and enjoyable !
title: A nice quick walk

body: Wonderful quiet walk taking no more than 2 hours return. Small entrance road to start walk opposite town end of racecourse. Beautiful Buddhist temple not far from the top which is worth a visit. Very good road/path the whole way to the summit around 7000ft. Fenced off TV masts at summit. Altogether one of the nicest things to do in Nuwara Eliya for a bit of exercise.
title: Mr David

body: Like a previous reviewer said, this place is not well signposted. We weren't staying nearby and we had to ask for directions. No one seemed to know where this elusive hill was. We finally found Single Tree Road, which is also known as Scur State Road on Google maps. The entrance is right in front of the Nuwara Eliya Race Course grounds. Once we established we were on the right track, it was an easy walk up to the top, through a tea plantation. We brought sandwiches and had a picnic brunch with an amazing view. The kids found it fun.
title: Easy walk, even for young kids

body: You can see nuwaraeliya town very nicely from this mountain. There is a telecommunication tower top of the mountain. So no enterence for that area.but can see from other side. you can see best scenario of gregory lake from this mountain. There is a road (you can go by vehicle) until top of mountain towards telecommunication tower. Very nice and cold place.
title: About

body: Not very well sign posted. We ended up climbing like goat through the tea plantation and found an easier way down through a little Tamil village. Great views.
title: Great view but not easy access

body: This is the best place to see all Nuwaraeliya. Scenic view is almost feel like in the sky. There is no place like this. Nice route to Single Tree Hill through a healthy tea plantation. Cool climate makes the trip even better.
title: Best view over Nuwaraeliya

body: the view is absolutely breath taking. Many people hike there - however, we took the easy way out and took a cab. the road is pretty narrow - not a problem if you are gonna hike though.Once you reach the point, you can see the city spread around you, tea gardens etc.
title: Amazing Views

body: Hike lasts max 2 hours, starting from the Single Tree Road (who would have guessed). The road almost has no traffic, it's quiet. We did this after we visited Adams Peak the day before, and the hike was still doable. Funny is that you can see Adams Peak from the top,so if you're planning to go to Adams Peak or you just went there, it's nice to see it from another place as well. Underway you can visit a Buddha temple if you like. We didn't enter, but it looked good from the outside. On top you can see the lake, the horse track and various other things in town. Just take the small path on the right between the antennas and enjoy the view! A little bit further there is a small path to the left through some small trees. You'll end up in a tree plantation and can go through it to go down the hill. It's a nice path but with hindsight I would rather start in the tea plantation and then go downwards via the road, which is easier. Nice to do if you've got some hours left to do something!
title: Quite nice, easy walk
Nice view ...
body: This is the 9th highest peak of Sri Lanka.If you wants to go you have to travel from Nuwaraeliya city towards Badulla rd and you will find a small road towards Single tree hill after about 2,km.You have motorable road up to the top but it's fun and nice to hike.You are not allow to go to the top as there are some telecommunications towers.Once you go up it's fabulous view over Nuwaraeliya city, Gregory lake .You can take some beautiful pictures So If you come to Nuwaraeliya don't missSingle tree hill

title: Nice view
body: When we arrived there, it's raining and cold. We decided to stay in but when it's clear we went out and finding a free places to visit, a tuk tuk driver told us about this place, we love it. Only one place its free to visit and you have to go!.

title: Nice trekking and a view
body: Nice and easy trekking that takes no more than two hours return. It is quite a lonely way and we did it in a misty afternoon.At the summit there is no single tree but TV antennas instead, but doesn't matter, it is worth doing it as an alternative plan in a small town.
